med.title: Resource limits and timeout (#5)
med.body:
**Where:** `src/main.c:119-133`.

No limits: a permitted interpreter can fork-bomb or burn CPU and memory, and the parent waits forever. `clone()` is now in place but sets no limits yet.

**Fix:** `setrlimit` in the child before exec (`RLIMIT_NPROC`, `RLIMIT_CPU`, `RLIMIT_AS`) and add a timeout on the wait.

**Note:** H3 is fixed, so a timeout-killed child is reported as `128 + signal`, not success.

med.title: Isolation via namespaces and seccomp (#1, #2) — BIG
med.body:
Unsolvable by filtering. **#1:** any interpreter escapes (`bash -c`, `find -exec`, `kubectl` plugins). **#2:** "safe" commands still damage via arguments (`cat ~/.ssh/id_*`, `tee`). You gate the verb, never the object.

**Fix:** contain what the child sees and touches — PID/mount/network namespaces plus a seccomp filter; after M1 and M2.

**Progress:** `clone()` (`src/main.c:119`) passes only `SIGCHLD` — no `CLONE_NEW*` flags, no isolation yet.

med.title: Exit codes conflate rash and the child
med.body:
**Where:** `src/main.c`, all failure paths.

rash's own `EXIT_FAILURE` is indistinguishable from a child that legitimately exited 1, so callers cannot tell "rash refused" from "the command failed". Scripts and agents wrapping rash will misread denials as ordinary errors.

**Fix:** reserve a range for rash's own failures, in the 126/127 style, and document the codes.

med.title: Env allowlist passes caller-controlled values (was H8)
med.body:
**Where:** `src/config.c:64-81`.

The allowlist gates variable *names*, then copies their *values* from the caller's environment. Harmless today: rash grants no extra privilege and the config lists no loader variables. It becomes code execution inside whitelisted interpreters if someone adds `BASH_ENV`, `PYTHONPATH`, `PERL5LIB`, or `LD_*`.

**Fix:** hard-reject loader and startup variables at parse time, or let the config set fixed values instead of inheriting them.

low.title: Enforce log dir is root-owned & not group/world-writable (M8 residual; relates to M9)
Doc tripwire: if setuid returns, switch check_user to geteuid/getegid
low.body: No current bug — rash isn't setuid (07cdea6 backed it off), so getuid/getgid is correct today. This is a reminder to revisit check_user and drop privileges explicitly the moment setuid is reintroduced.

low.title: Verify config is root-owned & not group/world-writable at load (fstat the fd)
low.body: M9 was fixed operationally (chowned to root:root 644), but rash doesn't CHECK this at runtime — it trusts the file's ownership. The file was misowned as UID 644 once already, so drift happens; a runtime fstat makes the guarantee durable instead of relying on external state.

done.title: Non-string whitelist entry → wild pointer: fixed in `ede00ad` (ASan-verified).
Heap overflow on long `sysuser`: fixed in `9af433a` (ASan-verified).
A killed child reports success: fixed in `9af433a`.
Wrong-user denial is never logged: fixed in `9af433a`.
Uninitialized struct on parse failure: fixed in `9af433a` (ASan-verified).
Resolve the binary before exec (#6)
done.body:
**Where:** `src/main.c:28-36`, parent guard at `src/main.c:108`.

Absolute-path entries now `execv` the exact file (no search). With `syspath` unset, a parent guard denies any command lacking a leading `/`, so bare names can't resolve against the caller's cwd. With `syspath` set, `execvp` searches only that trusted, root-owned PATH.

**Nit:** the non-absolute denial hits stderr but isn't logged (`goto clear_2` skips `write_log`).

done.title: `conf.path` is never set
done.body:
**Where:** `src/config.c:91-101`, used at `src/main.c:28-36`.

`path` is now read from the config's `syspath` key and drives the child's PATH — or, when unset, selects the absolute-path `execv` mode (M1). No longer an uninitialized pointer, and PATH is config-driven rather than hardcoded.

**Watch:** if `syspath` lists a non-root-owned directory, the `execvp` search there is hijackable — keep it to root-owned dirs.

done.title: Memory leaks in `free_config`: arrays now freed unconditionally (ASan-verified, no leaks with an empty whitelist and unset env vars).
Dead code in `main`: unused `exitcode` and unreachable `retval = EXIT_SUCCESS;` removed; the Makefile now builds with `-Werror`.
clone failure only half-reported
done.body:
**Where:** `src/main.c:121-123`.

`clone()` failure now calls `perror("rash")` — good — but still writes no audit-log entry before cleanup. The caller sees a message, yet the log has a gap exactly when the system is under pressure, such as a fork bomb hitting limits.

**Fix:** `write_log` the failure with `errno` alongside the existing `perror`.

done.title: Audit log still lives in `/tmp` (was H4)
done.body:
**Where:** `src/main.c:61`, `src/main.c:72-80`.

`O_NOFOLLOW` now blocks symlink redirects, but the log is owned by the restricted user, who can edit or truncate it. With `fs.protected_regular=1`, another user pre-creating `/tmp/rash.log` makes `open` fail and rash refuses to run. Without `O_CLOEXEC`, children inherit a writable log handle.

**Fix:** log under a root-owned directory and open with `O_APPEND | O_CLOEXEC`.

done.title: Log successful executions ('ran %s') — was unreachable dead code, now reached
Config integrity (#4) (was H7)
done.body:
**Where:** `src/config.c:95`.

Not exploitable today: `hunterkiller` cannot write `/etc/rash/rash.toml` or `/etc/rash`. But the file is owned by nonexistent UID 644, likely a `chown`/`chmod` mix-up, so whoever later gets that UID controls the whitelist. rash never checks ownership before trusting the config.

**Fix:** `sudo chown root:root` the file; refuse to load unless root-owned and not group/world-writable, via `fstat` on the opened fd.

done.title: Feature macro centralized (-D_GNU_SOURCE in Makefile)
done.body:
[Deprioritized — Linux/glibc target, not chasing POSIX] **Where:** `src/main.c:1` (`_GNU_SOURCE`); `setenv` at `src/security.c:23`, `src/security.c:29`.

`main.c` defines `_GNU_SOURCE` (needed for `clone`), but `security.c` defines nothing and calls `setenv`, which isn't ISO C. Under `gcc -std=c99 -pedantic` it still fails with an implicit `setenv` declaration (confirmed). It only builds because gcc's default GNU mode exposes it.

**Fix:** set the feature macro once in the Makefile `OPTIONS` (`-D_GNU_SOURCE`, since `clone` needs it) rather than per-file.
